items.headline: FQ1 FY27 consensus EPS: $37.93 → $37.95 (+0.1%) — Nasdaq.com / Zacks
FY27 consensus EPS: $175.19 → $174.19 (-0.6%) — Nasdaq.com / Zacks
FY28 consensus EPS: $211.51 → $212.33 (+0.4%) — Nasdaq.com / Zacks
Mean price target: $1,621.67 → $1,624.42 (+0.2%) — Nasdaq.com / Zacks
MU closed $778.31 on 2026-11-13, +12.8% vs $690.00 on 2026-11-06 (Nasdaq.com official closes)

MU fell 2.52% on 13 Nov to close at $778.31 (from $798.44; range ~$750–$796, ~27.7M shares) in a broad chip sell-off as investors digested Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia; the stock was down as much as ~5.4% intraday and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell over 5% (Google Finance / ChartExchange, 2026-11-13)

HBM pricing power: industry sources say Huang's exit could give HBM makers (SK hynix, Samsung, Micron) more leverage with Nvidia; SemiAnalysis (third-party est.) sees SK hynix charging Nvidia $3.00–3.30/Gb for 2027 HBM4 vs $3.70–4.10/Gb for AMD, Broadcom, Amazon and Google, and Morgan Stanley (est.) sees Nvidia's share of HBM demand falling to ~37% in 2027 with Google ~36% (The Korea Herald (SemiAnalysis / Morgan Stanley estimates), 2026-11-13)

Memory sell-off: Micron and SK hynix each fell around 5% intraday and SanDisk about 8% on 13 Nov as Nvidia slid more than 4%; Saxo's Charu Chanana said further trouble at Nvidia would hit SK hynix and Micron most, though demand from other AI accelerator platforms could cushion the impact. Nvidia reports Q3 on Tue 17 Nov (US time) (Invezz (Saxo commentary), 2026-11-13)

Competitor supply discipline: Samsung and SK hynix are shifting to 'secure volume first, invest in stages', building clean rooms but pacing tool move-ins; SK hynix has 5-year LTAs with 14 customers covering over 50% of 2027–28 capacity (DRAM and HBM effectively sold out through 2029 incl. talks), while Samsung has multi-year deals with 10 large customers and is negotiating with 10 more, targeting 60–70% LTA coverage by 2030 (Hanyang Economy / Korea JoongAng Daily, 2026-11-13)

DRAM spot (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 13 Nov GMT+8): DDR5 16Gb 4800/5600 session avg $60.267 (+0.06%), DDR4 16Gb 3200 $79.50 (−0.31%), DDR4 8Gb 3200 $44.536 (−0.40%); DDRWatcher (est.) flags DDR4 spot down a fourth straight week (−2.7% w/w) and DDR5 −1.4% w/w, with module and contract prices still firm (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, 2026-11-13)
SEC filing: 144 (filed 2026-11-12)
SEC filing: 144 (filed 2026-11-12)

Insider filing: EVP & CBO Sumit Sadana filed Form 144 (12 Nov) for a proposed sale of 14,000 shares from vested performance shares (~$11.41M aggregate value, approx. sale date 11 Nov, via Morgan Stanley); his second Form 144 this week after 5,000 shares on 9 Nov. A Form 4 should follow (SEC EDGAR (Form 144), 2026-11-12)

MU slipped 1.59% on 12 Nov to close at $798.44 (from $811.30; range $764.57–$799.70, ~27M shares), recovering from an early drop of about 4–6% after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned (StockAnalysis / MarketBeat, 2026-11-12)

Largest HBM customer: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on 12 Nov after the board probe of his ties to an alleged Chinese spy; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. AI hardware stocks fell (MU was down ~5.8% pre-market, SK hynix ~3%), while AMD and Broadcom rose. No change to memory orders has been announced (CNA (Reuters), 2026-11-12)

Pricing: leading memory makers have reportedly told distributors verbally of new price hikes for enterprise-grade memory (DRAM contract and enterprise SSD); channel prices are already rising while consumer segments stay weak. TrendForce (third-party est.) expects Q4 enterprise SSD contract prices +15–20% (TrendForce (citing Lanjing News), 2026-11-12)

Competitor HBM4: SK hynix's HBM4 production yield has reportedly passed 70% (industry sources, not disclosed by the company); Samsung was said to be near 80% in September. Yield bases differ by vendor, so comparisons with Micron are not like-for-like (Chosun Biz, 2026-11-12)

DRAM spot (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 12 Nov GMT+8): DDR5 16Gb 4800/5600 session avg $60.233 (flat), DDR4 16Gb 3200 $79.75 (−0.15%), DDR4 8Gb 3200 $44.714 (−0.40%); DDR4 still drifting lower, DDR5 flat (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, 2026-11-12)

MU jumped 11.89% on 11 Nov to close at $811.30 (from $725.11; range $763.05–$827.58, ~35.5M shares) as CoreWeave's Q3 beat and raised outlook eased AI-spending fears; SanDisk rose about 11% and CoreWeave about 25%. MU then eased about 2% in after-hours trading (Nasdaq.com / The Motley Fool, 2026-11-11)

Customer demand: CoreWeave raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $13.0–13.3B (from $12.4–13.2B), guided capex of $37–39B and an exit run-rate of $20–21B; Micron has said more than 75% of its FY27 output is already committed (Benzinga, 2026-11-11)

Analyst lists: Bank of America removed Micron, Nvidia and Lam Research from its US 1 top-picks list on 10 Nov without giving a reason, but kept its Buy rating on all three (no rating or price-target change) (TIKR (Bank of America / Goldman Sachs), 2026-11-11)

HBM customer base: Google is expanding sales of its TPUs to outside cloud providers, widening HBM demand beyond Nvidia; Counterpoint (third-party est.) sees HBM bit demand for custom AI chips growing 35-fold from 2024 to 2028. The article focuses on Samsung and SK hynix supply (The Korea Herald (Counterpoint estimate), 2026-11-11)

DRAM spot (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 11 Nov GMT+8): DDR5 16Gb 4800/5600 session avg $60.233 (+0.11%), DDR4 16Gb 3200 $79.867 (−0.15%), DDR4 8Gb 3200 $44.893 (−0.24%); DDR4 still drifting lower, DDR5 flat (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, 2026-11-11)

MU slipped 1.10% on 10 Nov to close at $725.11 (from $733.15; range $699.63–$745.64, ~27.5M shares, about 32% below average volume) after an intraday dip of as much as 4.6% (Nasdaq.com / MarketBeat, 2026-11-10)

Korea follow-through: SK hynix (+6.8% to ₩1.213M) and Samsung (+5.9% to ₩201,000) jumped in Nextrade pre-market on 10 Nov after the US chip rebound (SK hynix ADR +5.5%) and a 4–6% drop in oil prices (Seoul Economic Daily, 2026-11-10)

Goldman Sachs (James Schneider, Neutral) reiterated its $1,250 price target (no change) and said risk/reward is becoming more attractive, with MU nearing tangible book value and a high probability of strong free cash flow in coming quarters; KeyBanc (John Vinh) also reiterated its $1,750 target on 9 Nov, citing October cloud data (TipRanks (Goldman Sachs note), 2026-11-10)

Competitor pricing (third-party reports): Samsung is reportedly asking Nvidia for HBM4 pricing at parity with SK hynix (reported mid-$500s per 12-high stack vs mid-$300s for HBM3E 12-high), with a deal expected before year-end; Reuters reported HBM-first allocation is squeezing legacy DRAM, with supplier inventories at two to four weeks (TrendForce) and Samsung keeping its DDR4 line running (Daily Silicon (citing Reuters / Global Economic), 2026-11-10)

Rumour check: a Korean report citing DigiTimes claimed Micron's HBM4 needed a redesign and could slip to 2027; Daily Silicon judged it overstated, noting Micron said at its 21 Oct webinar that HBM4 is in high-volume manufacturing and Nvidia confirmed all three suppliers in production for Rubin. No Micron statement on the new report (Daily Silicon (fact-check of ChoiceStock / DigiTimes report), 2026-11-10)

Strategic investment: Anthropic's updated IPO prospectus (10 Nov) shows Micron agreed to buy about $1.0B of Anthropic Class N stock (~13.5M shares at the $74 midpoint) in a $26B concurrent private placement alongside Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Microsoft and TSMC, at the IPO price and contingent on the IPO; Nasdaq debut expected 19 Nov (ticker ANT). No Micron 8-K on it so far (Reuters (via U.S. News) / Anthropic prospectus, 2026-11-10)

Demand mix (UBS, third-party est.): DRAM's share of 2027 AI-data-centre memory spending is seen at 74% (from 68% in 2026), with server DDR at 57% and HBM rising from 13% to 17%, while NAND falls from 32% to 26%; Samsung expects HBM to take ~30% of industry DRAM wafer capacity in 2027 (from ~20%) (Edaily (UBS estimate), 2026-11-10)
SEC filing: 144 (filed 2026-11-09)

MU rose 6.25% on 9 Nov to close at $733.15 (from $690.00; range $689.65–$744.74, ~31.9M shares) as chip stocks extended their rebound from last week's midterm-driven rout (SOX nearly +7%, AMD +13%), while Nvidia fell 4.3% (Nasdaq.com / The Motley Fool, 2026-11-09)

Insider: Form 144 (filed 9 Nov) gives notice that EVP and Chief Business Officer Sumit Sadana plans to sell 5,000 MU shares (~$3.65M, about $730/share) via Morgan Stanley around 9 Nov; the shares came from performance shares vested 13 Oct. He sold 15,000 shares on 18 Aug (~$14.0M). No 10b5-1 plan date given; the Form 4 is still to come (SEC Form 144, 2026-11-09)

Key HBM customer: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation after NYT/FT reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort through a relationship with a Megaspeed executive; NVDA closed −4.27% on 9 Nov (intraday −8.8%). Nvidia says it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised; no change to memory supply contracts has been reported (CNBC, 2026-11-09)

Morgan Stanley (third-party est., 9 Nov) told clients to buy the AI dip after the midterms, keeping hyperscaler capex forecasts at $1.6T for 2027 and $1.8T for 2028 (with downside risk to 2028); it expects about 20% of US data-center projects planned for 2028 (~5 GW) to slip into 2029 because of permitting friction in Texas and Ohio, and warns suppliers could face a 2028 downcycle if powered buildings become the bottleneck (investingLive (Morgan Stanley note), 2026-11-09)

DRAM spot (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, third-party, 9 Nov GMT+8): DDR4 8Gb (1Gx8) 3200 session avg $45.214 (−0.86%), DDR4 16Gb $80.236 (−0.72%), DDR5 16Gb $60.167 (flat); buyers make only price-probing inquiries. TrendForce Weekly Radar 009 says DRAM stays 'Very Tight' though lead times eased to 18 weeks (from 19), with US demand robust while Chinese buyers scale back (TrendForce / DRAMeXchange, 2026-11-09)

SK hynix told Aju Press no significant changes to supply arrangements or delivery schedules have emerged since the US midterms; its LTAs with 14 customers cover more than half of 2027–28 capacity, with quantities and timing adjustable only within agreed limits. Industry officials see an immediate memory-demand drop as unlikely (Aju Press, 2026-11-09)

Potential new supply (long-dated, unconfirmed): Elon Musk's Terafab reportedly told equipment makers it targets ~1M wafers/month by 2032, ~700K of them for memory (close to Samsung's ~650–700K DRAM wafer capacity), with mass production starting 2H28; memory partners and HBM/LPDDR split not disclosed (TrendForce (citing Nikkei / Financial News), 2026-11-09)

Post-midterm data-center regulation risk: Samsung says its 2027 HBM is sold out at negotiated prices and SK hynix says DRAM/HBM is effectively sold out through 2029 (LTAs >50% of 2027–28 capacity), but some analysts estimate about half of planned 2028 US data-center additions could fall under new permitting curbs; customers delaying acceptance could shift quarterly revenue even if volumes hold (Financial News (Korea), 2026-11-08)

Weekly DRAM spot (third-party, DRAMeXchange session averages, week to 6 Nov): DDR4 chips avg $47.81 (−1.0% w/w, third straight weekly fall), DDR5 $61.06 (−0.6% w/w, still +4.5% over 4 weeks, near its 40-week high); no contract-price reset seen (DDRWatcher (DRAMeXchange data), 2026-11-08)

The Information (6 Nov, two people familiar) reported TSMC has begun preparing plans to make 3D DRAM at Nvidia’s request, led by VP Hsu Kuo-chin (ex-head of Micron’s Taiwan operations), via a new fab or a converted plant; TSMC effectively denied it on 7 Nov, saying it stays a dedicated logic foundry. Winbond’s chair also sees in-house TSMC DRAM as unlikely (patents, process know-how). Unconfirmed report; any supply would be years away (Tom's Hardware (The Information report), 2026-11-07)
